summary:
Cantabria has no statute of its own on legal gender recognition or on anti-discrimination protection. The region stands under Spain's Ley 4/2023 of 28 February 2023, which applies uniformly across the country's autonomous communities, so a visitor to Cantabria deals with the same administrative route as anywhere in Spain: adults may rectify the registered sex entry on their civil registry record without prior surgical reassignment, the right being grounded in the free development of personality under Article 10.1 of the Spanish Constitution.

The same statute defines and sanctions discriminatory conduct and harassment on grounds of sexual orientation, sexual identity, gender expression and sexual characteristics, declares discriminatory contract clauses null and void, obliges the collection of discrimination data broken down by those causes, and mandates measures adapted to rural circumstances. Cantabria's position on these matters is therefore entirely derivative of the national framework; no regional instrument supplementing or narrowing it was identified.
tangentialFactors: No Cantabria-specific turbulence was identified in the source inventory: there is no record of regional legislative attempts to amend, restrict or delay the application of the national framework, and no record of regional political hostility toward trans people. The region's exposure to risk is the national one, with nothing in the sources indicating that enforcement or official attitudes in Cantabria diverge from the Spanish average in either direction.
localsOnly: Residents of Cantabria use the same Civil Registry route as the rest of Spain, with no additional regional precondition, waiting period or medical requirement documented in the sources. The national statute's mandate for measures adapted to rural circumstances is directly relevant to residents outside Santander, though the sources do not describe how the Cantabrian administration has implemented it.
outOfScopeNotes: Unresolved and not sourced: no Cantabria-specific data was identified on hate-crime or hate-speech incidents motivated by gender identity or expression, on how regional courts or the Policía Nacional and Guardia Civil apply the discrimination aggravating circumstance here, or on complaints about facility access. The region's health service, its practice on trans-specific healthcare, and the handling of gender-marker requests by Cantabrian registry offices are likewise not covered by the inventory. Whether any regional anti-discrimination instrument exists below the national layer remains unverified.
